producer_report.summary: Athena::go now publishes the admitted candidate when verification starts: it pushes it to athena/<job> and opens or reuses the job's PR through an EarlyPush seam (go keeps its signature; go_with_early takes the seam; GhEarly builds its own GhCli). It never merges and is skipped silently without a GitHub origin. Any failure becomes one warning, and the job outcome is unchanged. Branch writes are limited to a missing branch, a fast-forward, or the early head recorded in a pr-early-head marker. Landing swaps that early head for the landing commit through a new Remote::replace (git guarded push, check_replace first), sets link.head to the landing commit, reuses the PR, and merges guarded by it. Tests and a changelog entry are added."]

criteria_check.criterion: A fake-host test shows that when verification starts in Athena::go, the candidate is pushed to the job's PR branch and the PR is opened or updated via Remote::push and PrHost::open_pr before verification completes, with no merge call. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: run_pin_tests::verification_start_pushes_the_candidate_and_opens_the_pull_request_before_the_verifier_without_merging: shared log orders push < open_pr < verifier, one each, no merge, branch athena/<job>, commit exists in repo. Passed; fails when the early call is disabled (mutation run).

criteria_check.criterion: A fake-host test shows that a failing early push or early open_pr leaves the job's outcome identical to the no-failure case (job does not fail; land proceeds as today). Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: run_pin_tests::a_failing_early_push_or_open_pr_leaves_the_jobs_outcome_as_it_was compares state and reason across success, failing push and failing open_pr (Landed in all); exactly one warning with the injected text.

criteria_check.criterion: A test shows land still pushes the landing commit to the same branch, reuses the early PR (no second open_pr), uses the lease-pinned replace through check_replace, sets link.head to the landing commit after the replace and before the head check, and merges guarded with the landing commit (merge_heads == [L]). Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: gh::tests::landing_reuses_the_early_pull_request_and_swaps_the_early_head_under_a_guard (opened==1, one guarded replace (branch, land1, expected cand1), link head land1, checks only on land1, merge_heads==[land1]); landing_after_a_failed_early_open_... covers the publish path (two pushes, one PR). The explicit before-head-check ordering is not separately asserted.

criteria_check.criterion: A test runs go with no origin or a non-GitHub origin and shows the early step is skipped silently: no output line contains 'warning'. Only a host error on a GitHub remote prints a warning. Run: cargo test --workspace.
criteria_check.evidence: gh::tests::the_early_step_is_silent_with_no_origin_or_a_remote_that_is_not_github runs the real GhEarly on both (no output); a_host_error_on_a_github_remote_is_one_warning_and_nothing_else and a_failing_push_on_a_github_remote_is_one_warning_too show the single warning. Existing go tests run with the real GhEarly in origin-less repos.

criteria_check.criterion: cargo test --workspace (including the existing CLI lifecycle tests, with no new 'warning' line), cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets, and cargo fmt --check all pass clean. Each new test fails without the new behavior.
criteria_check.evidence: clippy -D warnings and fmt --check clean; cargo test --workspace --locked returned without an error exit code (output unreadable). Only the go-level mutation was run (early call disabled, test failed); I did not mutate replace_early_head.

criteria_check.criterion: The production early-push implementation builds its own GhCli runner, so the Athena::go signature and CLI call sites are unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: GhEarly::start builds GhCli and GitRemote itself; go(&self, job_ref, accepted_by, ui) is unchanged and delegates to go_with_early; no change under crates/athena-cli.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md says verification start opens or updates the job's PR so CI caches by fingerprint, that it never merges, that a missing or non-GitHub origin is skipped quietly, and that failures are non-fatal.
criteria_check.evidence: New entry under Unreleased/Added in CHANGELOG.md states all four points.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: the go-level tests are in run_pin_tests.rs (not a listed deliverable) because the go scaffolding lives there; land.rs, lifecycle.rs and test_support.rs are unchanged on purpose.
The 'link.head set before the head check' ordering is exercised by the end-to-end land test but not asserted as a separate step.
No hard timeout on git push or ls-remote beyond GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and the host client's bounded retries.
The early PR body is written at verification start and land does not rewrite it (assumed acceptable).
mistakes: My first publish-path test used an ancestry fake that denied a commit is its own ancestor; fixed with an OnlyItself fake.
I could not read the saved full-suite output, so the workspace result rests on the missing error exit code.
learnings: Remote replace already existed in athena-git (push_if_remote_at) and check_replace in pr.rs; only the Remote trait method and the land flow were missing.
The word 'lease' is forbidden in files; athena-git spells the flag in two pieces. I used only 'guarded'.
clippy::too_many_arguments (7) forced bundling accepted_by and early into a tuple for dispatch.
Study-capability go tests in run_pin_tests.rs land in a temp repo with no origin, so the real GhEarly skips silently there.
desires: Permission to read tool-result output files so a long test run's result can be confirmed.
